changelog: Insert a discrete question about single obligatory heads/complements to correct the understating of risk when the right fragment supplies the sole element that completes or flips the left (addresses finding 1).
Insert guidance about separation of noun heads, titles, determiners or appositives to raise cohesion penalties when modifiers are orphaned (addresses finding 2).
findings: The prompt understates the risk when the right-hand fragment supplies the single obligatory element (a finite verb, nominal head, required complement, or explicit negation/reverser) that completes or sets the truth-conditions of the left; cutting there leaves the left fragment misleading or effectively contradicted when the right is heard alone.

The prompt undervalues cohesion damage when a cut splits a noun phrase or apposition — i.e. separates a title/role, determiner, or modifier from the name or head noun it attaches to — producing orphaned modifiers or unnatural name translations.

diagnosis.why: The new checks made the model move many cuts earlier in the sentence (hurt most for mid-length pieces, ≤7–≤10 words) so it began slicing off complements and list items instead of keeping them attached to their heads; this produced the large negative moves in the worst examples while slightly improving very-short bins (≤3). The wording for the single-obligatory-element check was interpreted as encouraging isolation of the completing element on the right, and the noun-head/apposition guidance caused the model to avoid some noun-boundary cuts by shifting cuts into predicates and enumerations.
diagnosis.lesson: When revising, ensure checks discourage cutting between heads and their obligatory complements/appositions (don’t encourage isolating the completer on the right) because otherwise the model will shift cuts earlier and fragment predicates and enumerations, especially harming mid-length pieces.
